Abstract.AbstractText: Obesity, insulin resistance, diabetes, and metabolic syndrome are associated with lipid alterations, and they affect the risk of long-term cardiovascular disease. Despite significant progress in medicine almost 400 million people are diabetic. Abdominal obesity is the reason for about 60% of heart attacks in western Europe. A reliable analytical instrument, not only to detect changes in the composition of lipids or their structures, but also the techniques or methods which will assist us to connect changes in a specific group of lipids with a specific disease and its progress, is constantly lacking. Lipidomics is a new field of medicine based on the research and identification of lipids and lipid metabolites present in and produced by human tissues, cells and body fluids. The primary aim of lipidomics is to search for new biomarkers of different diseases, mainly civilization diseases. This new approach in medicine also allows used therapies to be improved through the individual treatment of patients and the proper adjustment of drugs. The lipid group contains around 1.7 million species; they are totally different, in terms of the length of alifatic chain, amount of rings, additional functional groups such as sphingoid, sugar, phosphate, nitrogen base, or lack of thereof. Some of them are so complex that their complex analyses are a challenge for analysts. The qualitative and quantitative analysis of lipids is based mainly on mass spectrometry (MS). Features, which make MS the dominant analytical technique for lipids will be presented on the pages of this overview.
